title: Finite-stage Verdier biduality
statement:
Let $Y$ be a separated finite-type scheme over
$k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, and let $A=A_{E,n}$.
On either the small etale site or the small pro-etale site,

$$
D_Y=R\mathcal Hom_A(-,\omega_Y),\qquad \omega_Y=Ra_Y^!A,
$$

is a contravariant exact anti-equivalence of $D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$,
and the natural map $\delta_K:K\to D_YD_YK$ is an isomorphism.
No boundary duality input is a hypothesis of this theorem.

proof.text:
Work throughout at the finite coefficient stage $A=A_{E,n}$, with $n\ge1$ and $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$. On the etale site [lem-weil-verdier-preservation-strata] preserves $D^b_{ctf}$; applied to the constant free rank-one sheaf $A_Y$ of Tor interval $[0,0]$, it also makes $\omega_{Y,\mathrm{et}}=D_{Y,\mathrm{et}}A_Y$ bounded constructible and finite-Tor. The natural double-dual map is an isomorphism and the duality is an exact anti-equivalence by [thm-weil-etale-geometric-biduality].

Put $F=\nu_Y^*$. Clause (ii) of [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin] gives a bounded constructible etale representative $K'$ of each bounded constructible pro-etale $K$. Clause (ii) of [lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude] reflects its finite Tor interval to $K'$, and clause (i) preserves the interval of each etale finite-Tor object under $F$. Thus these equivalences restrict to the two $D^b_{ctf}$ categories.

Apply [lem-weil-finite-duality-site-comparison] with first argument $K'$ and second argument $\omega_{Y,\mathrm{et}}$, whose bounded constructibility was just verified. Together with its dualizing-object comparison this gives natural isomorphisms $c_{K'}:FD_{\mathrm{et}}K'\xrightarrow{\sim}D_{\mathrm{proet}}FK'$. Hence the pro-etale dual is finite-Tor constructible, since the etale dual is and $F$ preserves finite Tor amplitude. The same comparison applies to $D_{\mathrm{et}}K'$. Its stated compatibility with evaluation and transposes identifies the pro-etale double-dual map with
$$
FK'\xrightarrow{F\delta_{K'}}FD_{\mathrm{et}}D_{\mathrm{et}}K'\xrightarrow{c_{D_{\mathrm{et}}K'}}D_{\mathrm{proet}}FD_{\mathrm{et}}K'\xrightarrow{D_{\mathrm{proet}}(c_{K'}^{-1})}D_{\mathrm{proet}}D_{\mathrm{proet}}FK'.
$$
Each arrow is invertible. Naturality gives the result for $K\cong FK'$. Finally the comparison lemma states that finite-stage Verdier duality is transported from etale duality: under the preceding equivalence and $c$, the exact contravariant anti-equivalence on the etale category is the pro-etale dual functor. The pro-etale exceptional inverse image here is exactly the comparison-class transport specified in that lemma, so no ambient pro-etale adjoint on arbitrary complexes or boundary-duality input has been assumed.
